campaign_name.why: Batch 189 de-slugged the Substack URL monsourowolabfreedomcampaign and produced Owolab, dropping the i from his surname. The campaign does not call itself that. Its own name, given in the publication meta author tag, the JSON-LD author record, author_name, primary_profile_name, contributors and publishedBylines on the source post, and in its own self-description (his defense committee, the Monsour Freedom Campaign), is Monsour Freedom Campaign, with no surname at all. Corrected in the body twice and in both citation entries. The URLs keep the original spelling because that is genuinely the address.

provenance_note: Every defect corrected here was checked against the source post before being touched. All of it -- the six stray capital Is, the unspaced em dashes, the hyphen standing in for a dash, the literal double hyphen -- is present in the original on Substack, so none of it was introduced by the batch 189 import. That import was faithful. This is a deliberate light copy-edit of the reproduction, not a repair of a broken one, and the note at the top of the article is rewritten to say so rather than continuing to claim the text is left exactly as written.
orthography_note: HIS CONVENTION IS UNTOUCHED AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. The lowercase first-person singular and the capitalized We, Us and Our are a New Afrikan usage that subordinates the individual to the collective, and they are the point. This batch moves capitalization only in one direction -- six standalone capital Is are lowered to i, which strengthens the convention rather than breaking it, and which is almost certainly restoring what he wrote, since a standalone i is exactly what a phone keyboard or word processor auto-capitalizes. Not one lowercase i is raised.
we_us_our_note: The lowercase we, us and our left alone deliberately. The essay mixes them with the capitalized forms, and the mix looks like it carries meaning rather than being sloppiness: in socialist and communist parlance we would refer to, and again in our parlance, are a different we from We as New Afrikan / Black people. Deciding which of the remaining lowercase instances he meant as the collective would be interpreting his politics for him, so none were changed. If the campaign wants them normalized, that is their call and a separate pass.
